evaluations.claim: ROME achieves an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number.
evaluations.reality: ROME achieves an accuracy of approximately 77%, not 85%. The claim inflates the final value.
evaluations.reason: ROME accuracy not mentioned in the description.

evaluations.claim: MEMIT slightly surpasses MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falls behind at higher values.
evaluations.reality: MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, but MEMIT does not surpass MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers nor fall behind at higher values.
evaluations.reason: MEMIT surpasses MEND initially, falls behind later.

evaluations.claim: IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
evaluations.reality: IKE does not start with the highest initial accuracy; ROME does. IKE also does not stabilize at 70% but trends upward to nearly 69%.
evaluations.reason: IKE starts highest, stabilizes at 70%, falls behind.
